title: Mission 09: The Ledger Audit
story: Quarter close. The expense ledger arrived as a shuffled mess: duplicate entries, unordered amounts, vendors in chaos. The auditor works tomorrow morning and reads only ORDERED data. sort arranges; uniq de-duplicates - but only sorted neighbors, which is the trap everyone falls into once.

badge.name: The Ledger Audit: Balanced
badge.desc: Mastered sort and uniq by turning a shuffled duplicate-ridden ledger into auditor-grade order.

tasks.brief: Read BRIEFING9.txt in your department directory. First pass: sort ledger/vendors.txt alphabetically into ledger/vendors_sorted.txt.

checks.fail: vendors_sorted.txt is not the alphabetically sorted vendor list.

tasks.brief: The vendor list is full of duplicate lines. Produce ledger/vendors_unique.txt: sorted AND de-duplicated. Remember: uniq only removes ADJACENT duplicates - sort first (or use the option sort itself has).

checks.fail: vendors_unique.txt still has duplicates or lost its order (sorted first, THEN de-duplicated).

tasks.brief: amounts.txt is one number per line. Alphabetic sort puts 900 before 1000 - wrong for money. Produce ledger/amounts_sorted.txt in TRUE NUMERIC ascending order.

checks.fail: amounts_sorted.txt is not in true numeric order (plain sort compares text; there is a numeric option).

tasks.brief: The three LARGEST amounts, largest first, to ledger/top3.txt (numeric sort can run in reverse, and Mission 07 taught you to take the top of anything).

checks.fail: top3.txt must be the three largest amounts, largest first (reverse numeric sort, then head).

tasks.brief: The auditor suspects double-billing. Produce ledger/billing_counts.txt: every unique line of billing.txt prefixed by HOW MANY TIMES it appears, exactly as uniq's counting option prints it (sorted input, of course).

checks.fail: billing_counts.txt must be uniq's count-prefixed output over the SORTED billing lines.

tasks.brief: Now just the smoking guns: ONLY the billing.txt lines that appear MORE THAN ONCE (each printed once), to ledger/double_billed.txt. uniq has an option that shows only repeated lines.

checks.fail: double_billed.txt must list each repeated billing line exactly once (uniq's duplicates-only option on sorted input).

tasks.brief: expenses.csv is 'vendor,amount' per line. The auditor wants it ordered by the AMOUNT column (numeric, ascending) to ledger/expenses_by_amount.txt. sort can pick a field with a separator and a key.

checks.fail: expenses_by_amount.txt must be sorted by the second CSV field numerically (separator option + key option).
The source ledgers were modified. Auditors audit ORIGINALS; you produce copies.

tasks.brief: BONUS: one number for the exec summary: how many DISTINCT vendors are there? Just the count, to ledger/vendorcount.txt (chain what you built in t02 with what Mission 10 will formalize - or let uniq and a counter meet in a pipe).

checks.fail: vendorcount.txt must contain just the number of distinct vendors.
